names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 3 august, «Sfântul Cuvios Dalmat», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 3 Αυγούστου, «Όσιοι Δαλμάτιος, Φαύστος, και Ισαάκιος», with the rank word and the two companions left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s first heading for the Julian 3 August, „Преп. Исакије, Далмат и Фауст.“ — Преп. left off, which governs all three names in it and which §5 maps to `venerable`. The heading gives no see, no city and no by-name, so the bare forename is the whole of the form; `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it folds with nothing.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 3 august — «Sfântul Cuvios Dalmat»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 3ης Αυγούστου — «Όσιοι Δαλμάτιος, Φαύστος, και Ισαάκιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 3 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the entry is the same company of three the Romanian line keeps: «Οσιος Φαυστος, Οσιος Ισαακιος, Οσιος Δαλματιος». saint.gr dates the honour and not the man — «τιμήθηκε και από τη Γ' Οικουμενική Σύνοδο που συνήλθε το 431 μ.Χ. στην Έφεσο, στην οποία οι Πατέρες ανέδειξαν τον όσιο αρχιμανδρίτη» — and gives no year of birth and no year of death, so no `dates` object is proposed and the year of the Council is recorded in the life instead. The third of the three, `isaac-of-constantinople`, already carries a venerated Greek row on 30 Μαΐου, and this page cross-references it itself, «βλέπε 30 Μαΐου»; that row is left exactly where it is and nothing is drafted for him. The page adds two relics: a portion of Dalmatios's at Νέα Θηβαΐδα on the Holy Mountain, and a portion of Isaac's at the monastery of Κύκκος in Cyprus. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The apolytikion and the kontakion the page prints are both the company's and name all three; they are taken here and on `faustus-son-of-dalmatus`, and not on Isaac, whose row is not this reader's to touch.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 16.08.2026 (3. август ст. ст.) — „Преп. Исакије, Далмат и Фауст.“

attestations.note: The day’s first of four entries, and its heading enumerates three men: „Преп. Исакије, Далмат и Фауст.“, under one rank word that governs all three. His row was `undocumented`. **A CENTURY ON A FOLDER THAT HELD NO DATE AT ALL.** „Угодивши Богу представио се мирно, у V столећу.“ — having pleased God he reposed peacefully, in the fifth century — is written as `death` 401–500, display «5th century», basis traditional. Neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave this folder a year. **AND THE SAME SENTENCE CORROBORATES A ROW THIS READER WROTE SIX DAYS AGO.** „Свети Далмат беше најпре официр при цару Теодосију Великом, и цар га држаше у великој части.“ makes him first an officer under the emperor Theodosius the Great, held by him in great honour — and `theodosius-the-great` is `related` on this folder already, in both directions, so nothing is added; it is the same emperor the Julian 28 June related to `senuphius-the-standard-bearer`, and this is a second entry of the same book putting a saint of this corpus beside him. **WHAT ELSE THE ENTRY GIVES.** „Но када се у њему пробуди дух, он презре све светско, напусти свој чин, узе свога јединца сина Фауста, и с њим оде у предграђе Цариграда, у обитељ св. Исакија, где се обојица постригоше у иноке.“ has him despise the world, leave his rank, take his only son Faustus and go to Isaac’s house in the suburbs of Constantinople, where both were tonsured; „Доцније се та обитељ по Далмату назвала Далматска.“ has the house named Dalmatou after him; „Далмат се предаваше посту понекад и до 40 дана. И постом победи невидљиву силу демонску.“ has him fast sometimes up to forty days and conquer the invisible demonic power by fasting; „Участвовао на III Васељ. Сабору, и борио се против јереси Несторијеве.“ has him at the Third Ecumenical Council fighting the heresy of Nestorius. **`types` UNTOUCHED AND TWO BODY WORDS REFUSED.** Преп. is `venerable` and the folder has it; `abbot` and `presbyter` it has from the other two books. официр, an officer, is not in §5’s table at all — војник is, and this is not that word — and игуман would give `abbot`, which is there already. The Council is no folder and Nestorius is no folder. No `locations`: Constantinople is named in a clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person. The ПЕСМА is twenty-two lines on the third entry alone, Anthony on his rock „Мртва стена и човек на стени, Бурно море около се пени Антоније у Бога удубљен Ум свој Богу стално уздизаше И молитве срцем узносаше.“, and it is in no field and in no life (§3), read before this was written.

hymns.text: Dumnezeul părinţilor noştri, Care Te porţi pururea cu noi după blândeţile Tale, nu depărta mila Ta de la noi, ci, pentru rugăciunile părinţilor noştri, îndreptează viaţa noastră în pace.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinţilor Cuvioşi Isaachie, Dalmat şi Faust», Glasul 4 — the one troparion the site prints for the three of them

english.text: God of our fathers, who ever deal with us according to Your gentleness, do not take Your mercy from us, but by the prayers of our fathers guide our life in peace.

hymns.text: Τὴν τρίστιχον χορείαν τῶν Ὅσιων τιμήσωμεν, Φαῦστον Ἰσαάκιον ἅμα, καὶ Δαλμάτιον τὸν ἔνδοξον ὡς τρίφωτος λαμπὰς γὰρ ἀρετῶν, σκεδάζουσι τὴν νύκτα τῶν παθῶν, καὶ ταὶς θείαις καταυγάζουσι δωρεαίς, τοὺς πόθω ἀνακράζοντας, δόξα τῷ θαυμαστώσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ μεγαλύναντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν, πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος α’, Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιοι Δαλμάτιος, Φαύστος, και Ισαάκιος», and it names all three of the company, «Φαῦστον Ἰσαάκιον ἅμα, καὶ Δαλμάτιον τὸν ἔνδοξον»

english.text: Let us honour the threefold choir of the venerable ones — Faustus and Isaac together, and Dalmatus the glorious; for as a triple lamp of the virtues they scatter the night of the passions, and they shine with divine gifts upon those who cry out in longing: glory to Him who has made you wondrous, glory to Him who has magnified you, glory to Him who works healings for all through you.

hymns.text: Τοὺς ἐν ἀσκήσει ἐκλάμψαντας ἐν τῶ κόσμῳ, καὶ τὰς αἰρέσεις ἀνατρέψαντας τῇ πίστει, ὕμνοις, Ἰσαάκιον εὐφημήσωμεν, σὺν τῷ Δαλμάτῳ Φαῦστον, ὡς τοῦ Χριστοῦ θεράποντας, αὐτὸν δυσωποῦντας ὑπὲρ πάντων ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις — the second hymn on the page of «Όσιοι Δαλμάτιος, Φαύστος, και Ισαάκιος», and it too names all three, «Ἰσαάκιον εὐφημήσωμεν, σὺν τῷ Δαλμάτῳ Φαῦστον»

english.text: Those who shone out in the world by ascetic labour and overturned the heresies by faith, let us praise with hymns — Isaac, with Dalmatus and Faustus — as servants of Christ, entreating Him on behalf of us all.

death.note: The folder held no date: neither doxologia nor saint.gr gives it a year. The Охридски пролог for 3. август ст. ст.: „Угодивши Богу представио се мирно, у V столећу.“ — having pleased God he reposed peacefully, in the fifth century. The same entry has him an officer under Theodosius the Great and at the Third Ecumenical Council, both of which sit inside that century and neither of which is used to narrow it (6 October 2026).
